text:
maya: Heads up — partner X reported a bunch of offline usage that arrived late over the weekend. We lost visibility in the 1h -> 24h window and some entitlements didn't reconcile. Can we quick-sync on a mitigation plan?

elliot: Ugh. Do we have numbers on how much usage was impacted and which SKUs?

maya: Rough estimate ~22k tokens / ~1200 embedding units across 3 SKUs. Most hits landed between 02:00-04:30 UTC Sat.

nora: Partner says their aggregator buffers and then POSTs hourly. They saw a backlog and then a burst after they recovered. We need to decide whether to auto-credit or hold until match.

samir: Short-term idea: mark late arrivals with a header so downstream reconciler treats them as "replay" events and doesn't immediately credit. e.g. ``X-Redwood-Replay: true`` in the POST. Then we can run the matching job with different heuristics.

jen: Legal note — credits automatically applied might be ok but need invoice footnote. Holding until matched is safer for now. Also keep auditable logs.

elliot: Agreed. If we hold, ops needs a clear SLA for manual review so customers don't get blocked. Propose auto-ack now, but credit on confirmed match.

maya: Proposed runbook (short):
1) Immediately tag incoming late payloads as replay if their event_timestamp < now() - 1h.
2) Prioritize matching job: first pass fuzzy-match on event_id + device_id + approximate timestamp (±10m), second pass use payload hash.
3) If match found within 24h apply credit, otherwise queue for partner follow-up.
4) Create a replay-priority queue for ingestion so we don't starve real-time traffic.

samir: Implementation notes:
- Ingest service: accept header ``X-Redwood-Replay: true`` or compute server-side.
- Route to separate Kafka topic replay-usage.{region}.
- Consumer runs greedy-match with backoff.
- Metric: replay_match_rate, replay_lag_seconds, replay_queue_size.

ingest-bot: deploy scheduled: ingest-service:v2.14.3 -> rollout canary to us-west-2 tonight at 01:00 UTC. Use feature flag partner.replay_handling = on for partner X only.

nora: Tests: we should seed staging with synthetic bursts (10k events) and verify matching job keeps RT P50 under 200ms and replay queue drains within 6h.

elliot: Billing policy for credits: create a new transaction type "replay_pending" that shows on invoice as pending-credit. If reconciled, convert to credit line; if not reconciled in 30d, mark as disputed and notify partner.

jen: Sounds reasonable. Add requirement: all replay events must include original signed_fingerprint to validate authenticity for audit.

maya: Action items:
- samir: add header handling + topic routing (ETA tomorrow EOD)
- nora: coordinate staging test and partner sign-off (ETA +48h)
- elliot: draft invoice UX for pending-credit (ETA 3 days)
- jen: add legal note and required fields (signed_fingerprint) (ETA 48h)

samir: I'll open a PR for the ingest changes and add unit tests for header + server-side watermarking.

nora: I'll schedule a quick sync with partner X for Wed 10:00 PT and share test dataset.

maya: Great — once staging run looks good we'll flip feature flag and monitor replay_match_rate and any unexpected credit noise. :crossed_fingers:

elliot: Can we also add alert if replay_queue_size > 50k or replay_lag_seconds > 86400? That should escalate to oncall.

samir: yes, will add alerts to ops-dash and a PagerDuty rule for that threshold.

maya: Thanks all. I'll post this runbook to the partnerships playbook and ping legal/billing owners for signoff after their PRs.

ingest-bot: ticket created: IN-8271 "partner X replay handling + routing" assigned to samir.
